jobs.title: Principal Data Lead (Data Engineering with Full-Stack Dev)
jobs.description: Job Summary We are seeking a Principal Data Lead to set the technical direction of our Reference Data Platform - the system of record that masters, governs, and distributes the firm's core reference data (parties, instruments, portfolios, and accounts). This is a hands-on technical leadership role: you will own the end-to-end architecture of a layered, event-driven data platform - spanning sourcing, ingestion, entity mastering, a bitemporal golden copy, and an API-first distribution layer - and drive it from vision to production. You will be the senior-most engineering voice on reference data, shaping platform strategy, establishing engineering standards across teams, and partnering with product, data, and infrastructure leaders to deliver a scalable, vendor-agnostic master data capability. The ideal candidate is an expert Python engineer and data architect with deep experience in master data management (MDM) and reference data within the financial industry - including market data and vendor feeds - combined with hands-on experience applying Generative AI to data platforms, distributed data processing, and building reusable, independently scalable platform components. Roles Responsibilities Own the architecture of a layered reference-data platform, defining the contracts between sourcing, ingestion, mastering, golden-copy, and distribution layers so each is independently buildable, deployable, and scalable. Set technical direction for entity mastering - standardization, blocking, matching, survivorship, and crosswalk/lineage - designing rules as configuration (data, not code) that scale from exact-match fast paths to full-population fuzzy resolution. Architect the durable golden copy: a bitemporal, point-in-time source of truth with match evidence, per-attribute provenance, and a schema-last serving model that adapts to new sources and domains without migration. Define the event-driven backbone and cadence model (start-of-day, intraday, end-of-day, and on-demand) enabling batch today and real-time streaming (CDC / Kafka) without re-architecture. Design the API-first, self-documenting distribution surface (REST, curated data products, subscriptions) governed by data contracts and consumable by applications, analytics, and AI/agents. Drive the platform's storage and compute strategy over an open lakehouse (Apache Iceberg, Snowflake) and elastic compute (Spark), ensuring an open, vendor-agnostic, no-lock-in foundation. Establish engineering standards, reference patterns, and a reusable component library (a layered monorepo) that make capabilities build-once, reuse-everywhere across domains. Lead cross-team technical design reviews, resolve the hardest architectural trade-offs, and align engineering execution with the firm's data strategy. Champion data quality, governance, security, entitlements, audit, and observability as first-class, cross-cutting foundations of the platform. Mentor senior and staff engineers, grow technical depth across the team, and set the bar for engineering excellence. Partner with product and business stakeholders to translate reference-data needs into a durable, scalable platform roadmap. Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 12+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant time as a technical lead or architect of data-intensive platforms. Expert-level proficiency in Python for building production services, data pipelines, and platform frameworks. Proven experience architecting master data management (MDM) or reference/entity-data systems - entity resolution, survivorship, golden records, crosswalk, and lineage. Deep data engineering expertise: data modeling, ETL/ELT design, distributed processing (Spark), and data distribution patterns at scale. Hands-on experience designing API-first services and event-driven / streaming architectures (e.g., Kafka, CDC). Strong command of modern data storage - relational, non-relational, and lakehouse formats (e.g., Apache Iceberg) - and SQL. Experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and cloud-native deployment (containers, Kubernetes/EKS, CI/CD). Deep domain experience with reference and master data in the financial industry - parties / legal entities, instruments, portfolios, and accounts - and the identifier, hierarchy, and cross-referencing challenges specific to it. Hands-on experience integrating and mastering market data and vendor/administrator feeds (e.g., Bloomberg, exchange, and fund-servicing sources), including normalization, cross-referencing, and point-in-time handling. Practical experience applying Generative AI / LLMs to data platforms - e.g., grounded retrieval over governed data, entity-resolution and data-quality assistance, or AI/agent-ready data access with provenance guarantees. A track record of setting technical direction, driving architecture across teams, and mentoring senior engineers. Excellent judgment on architectural trade-offs, and the communication skills to align engineering, product, and business stakeholders. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with bitemporal / point-in-time data modeling and governed, auditable data systems. jobs.title: Sr Full stack developer
jobs.description: Job Summary Youll join a small, senior team building a multi-tenant operations platform for MSPs. The platform sits between the systems our partners already run their businesses on - PSA platforms like ConnectWise, HaloPSA, and Autotask - and layers on AI-driven analytics, customer health scoring, revenue intelligence, and a real-time ticket synchronization engine. This is not a CRUD-app job. The core of the work is synchronization: keeping thousands of ticket pairs, notes, time entries, and attachments consistent across systems we don t control, with rate limits, flaky webhooks, and partners who expect zero data loss. On top of that data, you ll build the dashboards and analytics that make it useful. Small team, real ownership, and a product where correctness is the feature. If you like problems that stay interesting after the first week, this is one. Responsibilities Build and maintain the ticket sync engine - bidirectional ticket, note, time-entry, and attachment sync across ConnectWise, HaloPSA, Autotask, and ServiceNow, with webhook-first delivery, polling fallback, idempotency, and loop prevention. Design Postgres schemas and Row-Level Security policies that enforce strict per-tenant isolation inside a shared database. Ship React + TypeScript features - operational dashboards, admin configuration panels, and partner-facing analytics. Write and deploy serverless functions (Deno/Edge) for webhooks, scheduled jobs, and AI batch pipelines. Own data quality: deduplication, conflict resolution, drift detection, and self-healing reconciliation. Instrument everything - structured logs, job queues, dead-letter handling, and operational runbooks. You will be on call for the systems you build. Document what you ship. Every feature gets KB documentation. This product is sold on trust, and trust is written down. Must-haves React 18 + TypeScript 5 in real production apps. You can reason about data fetching, caching, and render performance without hand-waving. Postgres at depth. RLS policies you ve actually written, SECURITY DEFINER functions, partial and expression indexes, window functions. You ve debugged a recursive RLS policy and won. Supabase in production (or an equivalent Postgres + auth + storage stack), including auth flows, edge functions, and cron scheduling. Distributed-sync instincts. You can answer, without notes: two systems update the same record - how do you avoid duplicates and loops and a webhook and a poll race each other - what breaks API hardening. You ve integrated third-party APIs with pagination quirks, picklist validation, rate limits, and permission errors - and you read the docs closely enough to know that net_total isn t what it says it is. Production discipline. You validate every migration for regressions, write tests for sync edge cases rather than happy paths, and push back when a request will break something. Git fluency for managing a shared codebase. Branching and merge strategy, meaningful commits and readable history, rebasing without losing work, resolving non-trivial conflicts, and code review as a two-way conversation. You can bisect your way to the commit that introduced a regression, and you know how to revert safely in a live system at 2am. AI-assisted development as part of your normal workflow. You use tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot daily, and you can articulate where they speed you up and where they quietly cost you time. Clear written English and comfort working async with colleagues and partners in North America. Working with AI tools We build AI features, and we use AI tools to build. We re not looking for enthusiasm - we re looking for judgment. Concretely, that means things like: Scaffolding an integration client from a PSA vendor s API docs, then hardening it yourself for pagination quirks, rate limits, and permission errors the model didn t know about. Generating a test matrix for sync edge cases - duplicate webhooks, out-of-order updates, partial failures - and pruning the cases that don t reflect real failure modes. Drafting a migration or an RLS policy with a model, then reading every line before it touches a shared database. Orienting in unfamiliar code - summarizing a module or a vendor SDK before you change it, rather than instead of understanding it. Turning a merged diff into a KB article.
